study type: Tool development and validation study with cross-sectional data collection
outcome: Agreement between new and existing tools for anal incontinence detection
cohort: The study included health professionals and women who were pregnant or had recently birthed (Phase I), and 358 prenatal parous women attending a first antenatal appointment (Phase II).
finding: The developed Bowel-Screening Questionnaire is reliable and valid, effectively detecting anal incontinence symptoms, including a high incidence of bowel incontinence and identifying rectal urgency and flatus as precursors for worsening function.
cross-section timing: For Phase II, data was collected at the first antenatal appointment for prenatal parous women; for Phase I, data was collected from pregnant or recently birthed women.
